evidence_note: Cases catalog the books claims in own words; many rest on informants, photographs, and inference, so each case keeps its gaps visible.

cases.name: Astor
cases.pattern: Rise through lodge access and state privilege into fur, opium, land, and banking, then influence through press, foundations, and transatlantic institutions.

cases.name: Bundy
cases.pattern: Adviser, intelligence, and foundation placement, with a manufactured problem and managed solution used as the model case.

cases.name: Collins/Todd
cases.pattern: Hidden occult authority with council imagery, witness intimidation, and a prison-framing narrative showing retaliation against exposure.

cases.name: DuPont
cases.pattern: Dynastic secrecy, press management, cousin marriage, chemical monopoly, and state capture in one small state.

cases.name: Freeman/Prieure
cases.pattern: A guarded bloodline order with archives, grand-master succession, and presidential advisers as hidden instruction channels.

cases.name: Kennedy
cases.pattern: Surname frequency blocks simple identification, so the search shifts to intermarriage clusters and aristocratic branches.

cases.name: Li/Triad
cases.pattern: Territorial factions with public covers, strong-arm units, extortion, and infiltration of police and government.

cases.name: Onassis
cases.pattern: Shipping wealth and social access read as power channels, with sparse direct ritual evidence admitted in the text.

cases.name: Rockefeller
cases.pattern: Layered trusts and foundations funding seminaries, universities, media, and religious bodies into alignment.

cases.name: Rothschild
cases.pattern: Five brother-led houses in major capitals, family-only partnership, private couriers, coded correspondence, and finance as control over governments.

cases.name: Disney
cases.pattern: A wholesome family brand allegedly lowering audience guard, with a wordless music film catalogued as a foundation template case at abstract level only.

cases.name: Reynolds
cases.pattern: Foundation grant networks and interlocking directorates linking tobacco, banking, aluminum, and universities.

cases.name: McDonald
cases.pattern: Clan continuity claims and franchise diffusion, with a documented compensation report used as an evidence exhibit.

cases.name: Krupp
cases.pattern: Concealed rearmament through foreign front companies, scandal suppression, and trial reversal by an insider.

cases.name: Hypothetical structured system
cases.pattern: The book own worked example walks through layered access, numbered sections, and paired-card codes; explicitly hypothetical.

cases.name: Evangelist case
cases.pattern: Staff policy, referrals, memberships, and image management are claimed as a front pattern; anecdotal grounds, gaps visible.

cases.name: Pacifist-community cover case
cases.pattern: Secrecy culture and wartime hospital service are presented as an infiltration route; claim pattern only.

cases.name: Alien-script person cases
cases.pattern: Three person cases are read through alien-themed scripts as alleged cover narratives.

cases.name: Celebrity milieu case
cases.pattern: Fame, entourage, contracts, and public image are described as a control environment.

cases.name: Handler-death exposure
cases.pattern: Loss of a handler is presented as the moment control weakens and secrets surface.

cases.name: Hidden Hand series
cases.pattern: Portraits of presidents, soldiers, royalty, and financiers are presented as instances of one sign; intent inferred from pose.

cases.name: Fellow Craft series
cases.pattern: Religious and political figures are presented as displaying a penal sign; photo-based assertion, gaps visible.

cases.name: Bush sign controversy
cases.pattern: Inauguration and magazine photos argue a sports explanation is insufficient for repeated family sign use; ambiguity unresolved.

cases.name: Nixon resignation
cases.pattern: A final public gesture is interpreted as a dueguard and tied to a fall-from-power narrative.

cases.name: Morgan and Adams
cases.pattern: An exposer murder and anti-Masonic writings serve as the historical warning case for secrecy enforcement.

cases.name: Oval Office eagle
cases.pattern: Opposite-facing eagles on desk and rug are treated as a combined double-headed emblem in plain sight.

cases.name: History retouching
cases.pattern: Paired Soviet-era photographs argue purged figures were removed from images and archives.

cases.name: Emblem substitution
cases.pattern: Square-and-compass variants with substituted centers are read as doctrinal replacements.

gaps: Many claims rest on confidential interviews, unnamed informants, or inference rather than documents shown in the text.
Namesake ambiguity affects several family cases; similar surnames are not proof of relation.
OCR noise makes some names, figures, and dates unreliable as extracted.
Ritual descriptions are fragmentary: roles and symbols appear without procedures, durations, or safeguards.
Internal article page numbers restart; PDF page markers are the reliable locator.
Book 7 claims rest heavily on unnamed witnesses and assertion; medical and technical claims lack controlled evidence in the text.
Book 9 visual claims depend on photographs that text extraction cannot verify; intent is often inferred from gesture.
